name: Prism
description: Lightweight, extensible browser-focused JS highlighter with a plugin system

host-language.comment: Repository is overwhelmingly JavaScript; the v2 branch (2.0.0-alpha.1) ships TypeScript type declarations (types/index.d.ts) and uses TypeScript as a dev dependency, but the stable 1.x line is plain JavaScript.

repository.comment: Default branch is now v2 (in development); v1 lives on as the stable npm release line.

first-release.comment: GitHub repository created 2012-07-10 by Lea Verou (spin-off from Dabblet); the npm package was first published 2015-05-12.

latest-version.comment: Checked 2026-11-18. npm dist-tag latest = 1.30.0 (2025-03-10); a 2.0.0-alpha.1 prerelease was published 2026-09-08 under the alpha tag.

engine-model.comment: Grammars are objects of regex patterns (with greedy/lookbehind/inside options); the FAQ explicitly chooses regexes over a full parser.

regex-engine.comment: Token patterns are native JavaScript RegExp objects.

embedded-languages.comment: Homepage: "Highlights embedded languages (e.g. CSS inside HTML, JavaScript inside HTML)"; implemented via nested `inside` grammars in the markup language definition. Default bundle includes markup, css, clike, javascript.

language-auto-detection.comment: Language must be given via a `language-xxx` class or API argument; no content-based guessing.

filename-extension-mapping.comment: Only via the first-party File Highlight plugin (browser), which determines the language from the fetched file's extension; the core API has no extension lookup.

resumable-line-state.comment: Prism.tokenize operates on the whole text and exposes no per-line state.

incremental-reparsing.comment: Regex highlighter without a parse tree; re-highlights the full block.

semantic-distinctions.comment: Pure regex lexer; tokens such as `function` / `class-name` come from regex heuristics, not a syntax tree.

bundled-languages.comment: Checked 2026-11-18: prismjs.com lists "all 297 languages currently supported by Prism" (v1.30.0 site; may include some dialect entries). Core default bundle in Node loads only 4 (markup, css, clike, javascript).

grammar-format.comment: Plain JS objects of token patterns registered on Prism.languages.

grammar-ecosystem-compatibility.comment: Consumes only Prism-format grammars; no TextMate/tree-sitter import.

runtime-grammar-loading.comment: A language is just an object assigned to Prism.languages (with extend/insertBefore helpers); Node's loadLanguages() adds components at runtime.

lazy-grammar-loading.comment: Autoloader plugin "automatically loads the needed languages" in the browser; loadLanguages() in Node. v2 also exports per-language modules.

grammar-accuracy.comment: Solid for common constructs; Prism documents known gaps on nested constructs (JS template literal interpolation, Python f-strings with nested quotes, nested comments in Rust/Swift/Scala, Rust closure params). Grammars are hand-maintained, not tracking upstream VS Code/tree-sitter grammars.

bundled-themes.comment: Checked 2026-11-18 (v1.30.0): Default, Dark, Funky, Okaidia, Twilight, Coy, Solarized Light, Tomorrow Night. Many more in the separate prism-themes repo.

theme-format.comment: Themes are plain CSS files targeting token classes.

token-classification.comment: Documented standard token set (keyword, function, class-name, string, …) that themes guarantee; languages may use non-standard names but are advised to alias them to standard tokens.

css-class-output.comment: Output is HTML spans with `token <type>` classes; styling lives entirely in the theme stylesheet.

multi-theme-output.comment: Contested: qualifies only via swappable stylesheets — output is theme-independent class markup, so a light and dark theme CSS can be swapped (e.g. via media-query <link>s) without re-rendering. Prism offers no built-in dual-theme/CSS-variable API, and its themes are not scoped for coexistence.

public-token-api.comment: Prism.tokenize(text, grammar) is documented as "the most low-level function you can use", returning a token stream of strings and Token objects.

ir-kinds.comment: Token stream: array of strings and Token {type, content, alias}, where content may itself be a nested token stream. hast output is provided by third-party refractor, not first-party.

serializable-ir.comment: Token stream is plain-ish JS data (Token class instances) but has no documented serialization format.

theme-resolved-tokens.comment: Tokens carry only type/alias names; colours live in CSS themes.

source-offsets-in-ir.comment: Token documents no start/end offset or line/column fields (only an optional matchedStr copy).

custom-formatter-api.comment: No pluggable formatter interface. Hooks (e.g. `wrap`) let you alter the generated HTML spans' attributes, and you can walk Prism.tokenize output yourself, but there is no documented formatter extension point for non-HTML targets.

line-transforms-decorations.comment: Via first-party browser plugins (Line Highlight with data-line ranges, Diff Highlight, Line Numbers, Command Line, etc.). These act on the DOM/highlight hooks in the browser rather than on a portable IR.

output-formats.comment: Prism.highlight returns class-based HTML. No first-party ANSI/LaTeX/etc.; React rendering via third-party prism-react-renderer, hast via refractor.

streaming-output.comment: highlight/tokenize take the complete text; no incremental API.

native-dependencies.comment: Zero runtime dependencies in both 1.30.0 and 2.0.0-alpha.1.

synchronous-api.comment: Prism.highlight / Prism.tokenize are synchronous; an optional async Web Worker mode exists for highlightAll.

bindings-ports.comment: No well-known ports to other host languages. JS wrappers exist (refractor → hast, used by react-syntax-highlighter; prism-react-renderer) but are same-language integrations.

core-package-size.comment: Bundlephobia min+gzip of prismjs@1.30.0 main entry (core + default markup/css/clike/javascript) = 7,140 bytes (checked 2026-11-18). prismjs.com claims the bare core is ~2 KB min+gzip, ~0.3–0.5 KB per extra language.

throughput-tier.comment: speed-highlight benchmark (Prism 1.30.0, Node 26, M4, median of 9): Prism fastest among candidates on 1 KB inputs, within 1.42× of highlight.js on 16 KB, but ~2.1× slower than highlight.js on 128 KB; shiki-js 5–7× slower. chsm.dev (Jan 2025): Prism fastest, highlight.js ~2× slower, Shiki ~7× slower. Note non-candidate speed-highlight is ~1.7–3.3× faster than Prism.

initialization-cost.comment: Cold start (import + first highlight) measured at 8.6 ms in the speed-highlight benchmark (Prism 1.30.0, Node 26, Apple M4); benchmark authored by a competing library's maintainer.

monthly-downloads.comment: npm, 2026-10-18 to 2026-11-16. Inflated by transitive installs (e.g. documentation tooling).

last-release.comment: v1.30.0 (last stable). 2.0.0-alpha.1 prerelease published 2026-09-08 not counted.

maintenance-status.comment: Substantive commits on the v2 branch through 2026-11-17 (new languages, plugin fixes) and a 2.0.0-alpha.1 release in Sept 2026, though the last stable v1 release was March 2025. README: only security-relevant PRs accepted while v2 is in development.

documentation-quality.comment: Dedicated site with usage guide, extending guide, token reference, plugin pages, FAQ, known-failures, and JSDoc API reference; no v1→v2 migration guide yet, and the API reference is thin in places (hook names undocumented).

notable-users.value: Gatsby (gatsby-remark-prismjs), Docusaurus (via Prism React Renderer), refractor / react-syntax-highlighter; prismjs.com also lists MDN, Stripe, Drupal

bus-factor.comment: MAINTAINERS.md lists 5 maintainers (Lea Verou, Michael Schmidt, Golmote, James DiGioia, Jason Kurian); recent commits mostly by Dmitry Sharabin plus community contributors. Community project, no corporate backing.
